conflicts.fact: Italic or underline rule for writing scientific names: whether the genus and species are underlined together or separately
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says the name is written in italics or underlined separately. Lesson 6 says to underline each part separately when handwritten. Both agree, so this is not a real conflict, only a wording difference.

conflicts.fact: Local names given for maize, beans and mosquito in different languages
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 gives maize as mbembe/'ngano ya Kikuyu' and 'oduma' in Dholuo, and bean as 'oganda' in Luo. Lesson 6 gives 'oganda' as a name for maize ('Mahindi, mbembe, oganda, maize'). So oganda is a bean name in Lesson 5 but a maize name in Lesson 6.

conflicts.fact: Example scientific name for the chicken
conflicts.versions: Lessons 5 and 6 give Gallus gallus domesticus. Lesson 8 gives Gallus gallus.

conflicts.fact: Name of the second taxonomic rank
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 uses Phylum/Division and discusses why books differ. Lesson 4 uses only Phylum. The ranks are the same, so this is not a real conflict.
